title: M/s Rudransh Hotel and Resorts v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
coram: Sangeeta Chandra, J.; Amitabh Kumar Rai, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; petitioner to complete indemnity and charges; licensee to decide in two weeks.
headnote: A lessee's writ for mandamus to release a 33 kW commercial connection without the landlord's NOC was disposed of on the licensee's statement that it would give a fresh connection if an indemnity bond, charges and other formalities were completed. The Court allowed ten days for those steps and directed the Executive Engineer to take an appropriate decision within two weeks thereafter. It did not order release of the connection or hold that an owner's NOC is unnecessary.
facts: The petitioner runs Hotel Palatial at Gomti Nagar, Lucknow, on premises leased from respondent no.4 by a registered lease dated 22 October 2024, which permits an independent electricity connection. It applied for a 33 kW commercial connection. MVVNL's Electricity Urban Distribution Division insisted on the landlord's NOC and said a central-point meter stood installed, whereas a multi-point meter was needed for a separate supply. The petitioner sought mandamus to release the connection without the owner's NOC, and daily compensation under section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003.

holding_units.holding: Where the licensee is willing to release a fresh connection to a lessee on completion of an indemnity bond, charges and other formalities, the Court will not mandamus release or waive the owner's NOC, but will allow a short time for those steps and direct the licensee to take an appropriate decision thereafter.

not_decided.point: Whether an owner's NOC is a condition of releasing a tenant's independent connection
Whether a central-point meter bars a separate multi-point connection
Compensation under section 43 of the Electricity Act, 2003 for delay in releasing the connection
